codeReview.summary: The feature delivers substantial CLI parity work, but stream-mode count semantics and stdin robustness are not fully baseline-compatible.

issues.description:
`search_stream_count` ignores `--invert-match` and always prints counts for matching lines (`count > 0`). Baseline `ag` differs for stream `-c -v` (example: input `hello hello
world
foo
` with pattern `hello` yields `ag` output `1
1`, while rust-ag outputs `2`). This breaks VAL-CLI-001 stream count parity under invert mode.

Stream mode uses `read_to_string(...).expect(...)`, which panics on non-UTF8 stdin and exits with panic status. Baseline `ag` handles the same byte stream without crashing (example bytes `\xFFhello\n`, pattern `hello`, baseline exits 0 with match output). This is a parity and stability regression for stream behavior.
Test coverage includes file `-c -v` and stream `-c`, but does not include stream `-c -v`, allowing the stream invert-count mismatch to pass undetected.
